title: Letter informing Southwest Power Pool, Inc. that the 08/24/2026 filing of revisions to its Open Access Transmission Tariff etc. is deficient and requesting additional information within 30 days under ER26-3591.

documents.name: ER26-3591-000 Deficiency Letter.docx
documents.text:
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
WASHINGTON, DC  20426

OFFICE OF ENERGY MARKET REGULATION


In Reply Refer To:
Southwest Power Pool, Inc.
Docket No. ER26-3591-000

Issued:  October 21, 2026
				
Southwest Power Pool, Inc.
201 Worthen Drive
Little Rock, AR  72223-4936

Attention:  Emon O. Mahony

Reference:  Deficiency Letter

Dear Mr. Mahony:

On August 24, 2026, Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (SPP) submitted revisions to its Open Access Transmission Tariff (Tariff) to modify Conditional High Impact Large Load (CHILL) provisions to accommodate planned outages.  

Please be advised that the submittal is deficient and that additional information is necessary to process the filing.  Please provide the information requested below. 

SPP explains that, currently, under section 2.22.1(d) of Attachment AE of the Tariff, a CHILL can be curtailed when the sum of the available capacity of its supporting Resources is less than the CHILL.  SPP proposes to revise its Tariff to provide that a “CHILL will not be curtailed solely due to supporting Resource insufficiency” when its supporting resource takes a Scheduled Resource Outage that is scheduled at least 14 days in advance of the planned start time.  Please explain whether there are limitations on how long a CHILL can stay online while all or some of its supporting Resources are on a Scheduled Resource Outage or otherwise unavailable to the SPP Integrated Marketplace.

SPP proposes to incentivize Resources supporting CHILLs to be available during Emergency Conditions by allowing them to receive compensation for deferring Scheduled Resource Outages in certain circumstances.  Specifically, the proposed revisions state that “Scheduled Resource Outages for supporting Resources for a [CHILL] . . . are solely Qualified [for compensation] if, in addition to the criteria in this Section B, the Outage is rescheduled at the request of the Transmission Provider to make the Resource available in Emergency Conditions . . . and the Resource was made available. . . .”  SPP contends that this is the same compensation offered to other Resources on approved Scheduled Resource Outages. 
 
Please explain whether and, if so, how SPP will consider whether a Resource is supporting a CHILL in its determination of which approved Scheduled Resource Outage it will request to be rescheduled.  

Please describe the circumstances in which SPP will request that “the Resource [be made] available in Emergency Conditions.”  For example, please clarify whether a Resource supporting a CHILL would only be eligible for compensation if it rescheduled its approved Scheduled Resource Outage in Emergency Conditions.

Please confirm whether the circumstances in which SPP may offer compensation to a Resource supporting a CHILL are the same as for other Resources.  If not, please describe and support that difference.

This letter is issued pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 375.307 (2025) and is interlocutory.  This letter is not subject to rehearing pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 385.713 (2025).  A response to this letter must be filed with the Secretary of the Commission within 30 days of the date of this letter by making a deficiency filing in accordance with the Commission’s electronic tariff requirements.  For your response, please use Type of Filing Code 180, Deficiency Filing.  The information requested in this letter will constitute an amendment to your filing, and a new filing date will be established.  A notice will be issued upon receipt of your filing.

Failure to respond to this letter within the time period specified may result in a further order rejecting your filing.

Issued by:  Natalie Y. Tingle-Stewart, Director, Division of Electric Power Regulation – Central
